description: A four-panel composite of secondary-electron SEM micrographs of the lightweight Fe–Mn–Al–C steel 9Al-10Mn-1C annealed at 800 °C, all recorded at 20 kV with printed magnification and scale bars; no composition/temperature values are printed on any panel. (a) X1,000, 10 µm bar: a coarse cellular/colony structure in which fields of fine parallel striations (the cellular transformation product) meet smoother, darker regions, with a grain-boundary triple junction near the centre. (b) X5,000, 5 µm bar: the lower half shows a very fine cross-hatched, chevron-like modulated contrast, while the upper half contains coarse dark elongated rod- and plate-shaped particles in a matrix, separated by a vertical band of blocky particles. (c) X5,000, 5 µm bar: the cellular product resolved as intersecting bundles of parallel needle/plate lamellae at several orientations. (d) X10,000, 1 µm bar: highest-magnification view of the lamellar regions, showing bright parallel plates truncated by narrow dark gaps. The caption partitions the panels: (a, b) spinodal decomposition plus nano-sized κ-carbides, (c, d) cellular transformation giving κ-carbide + ferrite + residual-austenite lamellar structure; the caption's phase symbols are lost (printed as hyphens), and the visual content of (a) shows both products, so the panel-by-panel assignment cannot be confirmed from the pixels alone.

subfigures.description: 20 kV SEM micrograph, X1,000, 10 µm scale bar. Coarse cellular/colony structure: fields of fine parallel striations adjoining smooth darker regions, with a grain-boundary triple junction near the centre.

20 kV SEM micrograph, X5,000, 5 µm scale bar. Lower region shows a fine cross-hatched/chevron modulated contrast; upper region shows coarse dark elongated rod- and plate-shaped particles in a matrix, with a vertical band of blocky particles between them.
20 kV SEM micrograph, X5,000, 5 µm scale bar. Intersecting bundles of parallel needle/plate lamellae at several orientations, characteristic of a cellular lamellar product.
20 kV SEM micrograph, X10,000, 1 µm scale bar. Highest-magnification view of the lamellar regions: bright parallel plates separated by narrow dark gaps (lamellar spacing well below 1 µm).

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a SEM micrograph acquired at 20 kV with magnification X1,000 and a 10 µm scale bar, showing a coarse cellular/colony structure with fine parallel striations next to smooth darker regions.

Panel (b) is acquired at 20 kV, X5,000 with a 5 µm scale bar; its lower half displays a fine cross-hatched/chevron modulated contrast and its upper half coarse dark elongated rod- and plate-shaped particles.
Panels (c) and (d) resolve a lamellar structure of parallel needle/plate-shaped plates at X5,000 (5 µm bar) and X10,000 (1 µm bar) respectively, with plates separated by narrow dark gaps.
All four panels carry the same printed instrument legend format '20kV', the magnification, and a white scale bar; no composition, temperature or hardness numbers are printed inside any panel.

The caption states the figure is 9Al-10Mn-1C at 800 °C, with spinodal decomposition into (matrix) plus nano-sized carbides in panels (a, b) and cellular transformation into carbide + (ferrite) + residual-(austenite) lamellar structure in panels (c, d).

In the caption the phase symbols are lost/garbled and appear only as hyphens ('spinodal decomposition in - + nano-sized -carbides', 'residual -'), so the exact phase names κ-carbide, ferrite and austenite cannot be read from the supplied caption string and must be inferred.
The citing text states that at an 800 °C annealing temperature 9Al-10Mn-1C undergoes cellular transformation for most of the austenite fraction and spinodal decomposition for the remainder.

The citing text states that cellular transformation generated (ferrite) + (carbide) + residual-(austenite) lamellar phases, and that residual austenite was detected as portions of carbide lamellae, suggesting an incomplete reaction.

The citing text states that the 9Al-10Mn-1C microstructure obtained at 800 °C gained outstanding hardness values among the 9% aluminium alloys and that a detailed SEM analysis is given in this figure and in Table 6.

A caption-versus-pixel discrepancy: the caption assigns panel (a) purely to spinodal decomposition, but the pixels of (a) also show strongly striated cellular/colony features similar to those in (c), so both transformation products appear to coexist at this magnification.
